conjecture: Q484: supply the missing multiplication rule for Motegi's basis of K-theoretic factorial Schur P/Q-analogues -- the type B and C trigonometric weight functions WC_{N,n,r}, WB_{N,n,r} of arXiv:2610.15344. Motegi fully characterises the basis (triangular vanishing, diagonal evaluation as a product over positive roots, divisibility, Newton smallness, uniqueness, branching, orthogonality, all-cardinality biorthogonality) and never multiplies two of them. The opening brief proposed a type-A G_m puzzle with a reflecting edge; the census gate redirected the session to an interpolation route.
note:
PROVE 2026-10-15. The rule is proved in the FIXED-POINT ALGEBRA: V = functions on the 2^N specialisation points u = w_M, pointwise product. The specialised weight functions are a basis of V (triangularity + nonzero root-product diagonal), so structure constants exist and are unique; they vanish unless nu >= lambda and nu >= mu, satisfy a well-founded recursion, have closed root-product form at the extremal labels, and admit a closed 2^N-term localisation formula via Motegi's own explicit matrix inverse. TWO MEASURED NEGATIVES bound what a combinatorial rule could be: (a) the identity does NOT lift to functions of u (0/16 pairs at N=n=2); (b) the structure constants are NOT Laurent polynomials, and the failure locus is SHARP: they are Laurent if and only if |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= 1, a criterion matching 225/225 support-bound triples at N=2 and N=3 with zero errors either way. Smallest witness c^{(1,2)}_{empty,empty} at N=2, a simple pole on w1 w2 = 1, the root hyperplane of t_1+t_2 in Delta^+(C_2). So no puzzle-style monomial-weight count can exist at cardinality jump >= 2 in this normalisation (and a diagonal rescaling makes it worse, 29/30 -> 4/30), while on the jump <= 1 stratum a puzzle rule remains open. The brief's own fork is therefore resolved on the 'wrong normalisation' side, NOT against the G_m formal group. CENSUS GATE at position zero did three things: it retired the brief's pre-registered row-4 falsifier as unusable (R(u_i,u_j^{-1}) IS a type-A R-matrix at an inverted argument, so the u_j u_k coupling does not require a boundary piece); it located the real separation in row 3 (q free vs the q=0 five-vertex puzzle); and it found the brief's table carrying ONE row for TWO groups -- S_n on u (which MATCHES type A) versus W(X_N) of rank N on w (which does not, and which is the group whose inversion/ascent sets write the diagonal evaluation). Ninth instance of the one-coordinate-match instrument.

PROVE 2026-10-16 (Q488/Q492). The pre-registered gate CLOSED Q492 NEGATIVELY in under 30 minutes: Motegi's boundary-degeneration count is n-s, not n-r; n is gauge (stability); and the invariant residue |M|-|I| is a row-vs-column gap while the jump is a column-vs-column gap -- cardinality gaps in DIFFERENT SLOTS of the same matrix, a one-coordinate match. Session then went to the same object and PROVED one direction of Q484's measured criterion. MECHANISM: the candidate pole divisors (read off Motegi's diagonal root product) fall into four families, and they split by whether the divisor is a COLLISION of two of the 2^N specialisation points. w_a=1 (padding collision via stability), w_a=-1 (via Atilde(-w)=Atilde(w)) and w_a=w_b (literal collision) all admit a collapse Atilde_{M,I}|_D = Atilde_{tau M,I}|_D with tau(M)<M, which forces the recursion's numerator to vanish to matching order => NO POLE EVER, for all triples. The long-root divisors w_a w_b = 1 are NOT collisions (w_a^{-1} is not among the w_c or the padding 1's) and that asymmetry is the whole theorem. There a pole is created iff some pair deletion nu\{a,b} stays above both lambda and mu, which is EXACTLY jump >= 2 by a two-line cardinality argument -- and that is where the puzzling max() in the criterion comes from. Hence jump <= 1 => Laurent, PROVED. The mechanism predicts the exact pole DIVISOR, not just Laurent-ness: 20/20 at N=2 and 115/115 at N=3. Both pre-registered plants fire (P1 moves the pole to w_a^2=q, P2 to w_a w_b=q). Two precisely-stated gaps remain: the q-shifted family (verified, not proved) and the non-vanishing converse. NOTE on method: the jump criterion and a rival 'uncovered' criterion |nu\(lambda u mu)|<=1 BOTH predict 176/195 at N=3 but disagree on 12 triples -- the matching COUNT was not a matching SET, and computing the 12 decided it for the jump criterion 7/7. Q484's conj:locus stands.

Lemma 1: Motegi's order M >= I (s >= r and m_{s-r+j} >= i_j) is a partial order on the power set of [N]; transitivity by the index substitution j' = t-r+j. Needed because the whole argument is a well-founded induction along it.

Lemma 2: the specialised weight functions e_I : M -> Atilde_{M,I} form a K-basis of the fixed-point algebra V = K^{P([N])}; triangularity in any linear extension of >= plus nonzero root-product diagonal gives det = prod_I Delta_I != 0. Independently corroborated by Motegi's explicit inverse, by a different mechanism.

Theorem A: c^nu_{lambda,mu} != 0 implies nu >= lambda and nu >= mu, by well-founded induction along >= using only triangularity and Delta_nu != 0. This is the type B/C analogue of the classical nu contains lambda, mu. Measured 64/64 at N=2 and 512/512 at N=3, type C.

Theorem B (well-founded recursion solving the rule from Motegi's specialisations alone) and Corollary C (at any nu minimal in {kappa >= lambda, kappa >= mu} the coefficient is Atilde_{nu,lambda}Atilde_{nu,mu}/Delta_nu; if lambda >= mu then c^lambda_{lambda,mu} = Atilde_{lambda,mu}; and c^lambda_{lambda,lambda} = Delta_lambda, a product over positive roots). Cor C measured 10/10 at N=2 and 35/35 at N=3.

Theorem E: the identity holds only on the 2^N lattice points and does NOT lift to an identity between functions of u. Measured: fails for all 16 pairs at N=n=2, type C, at the generic point u=(11/4,7/5), w=(3/2,5/3), q=2/7. Existence statement, so one point suffices; graded computed because the witness is a machine computation.

Theorem F: the structure constants are NOT Laurent polynomials in general, and the failure locus is sharp. MEASURED CRITERION, agreeing on 225/225 support-bound triples at N=2 and N=3 with zero errors in either direction: c^nu_{lambda,mu} is a Laurent polynomial in w IF AND ONLY IF |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= 1. Laurent counts 29/30 (N=2) and 176/195 (N=3). Smallest witness: c^{(1,2)}_{empty,empty} at N=2 has a simple pole on w1 w2 = 1, the root hyperplane of t_1+t_2 in Delta^+(C_2). Not a diagonal-normalisation artefact: rescaling e_I -> e_I/Delta_I drops the Laurent count to 4/30 at N=2. Exact symbolic computation over C(q)(w), graded computed because the witness is machine-produced.

children.reason: Killed on two independent grounds. (1) CENSUS, row 3, before any code: the WZJ type-A G_m puzzle is the q=0 five-vertex degeneration (zero free deformation parameters) while Motegi's characterisation theorems have q free -- same formal group G_m, different point of the quantum parameter, so the puzzle cannot produce the objects his uniqueness theorem characterises. (2) MEASURED, after: a puzzle rule is a count of tilings with monomial weights and therefore yields a Laurent polynomial, but the structure constants are not Laurent polynomials once the cardinality jump |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) reaches 2 (node nonpolynomiality-and-its-locus, criterion measured 225/225 at N<=3). The kill is therefore STRATIFIED, not total: on the jump <= 1 stratum polynomiality holds and a puzzle rule is not excluded. Separately, the brief's pre-registered row-4 falsifier is RETIRED as unusable, not failed: R(u_i,u_j^{-1}) is a type-A R-matrix at an inverted argument, so the u_j u_k coupling does NOT imply a boundary piece is necessary, and no inference was drawn from it in either direction.

children.approach: the sharp open question this session produces: the structure constants are Laurent polynomials exactly on cardinality jump |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= 1 (measured 225/225 at N<=3) and acquire poles on positive-root hyperplanes at jump >= 2. So EITHER find a normalisation in which they are polynomial at all jumps -- no diagonal rescaling achieves it, since the correction is multiplicative in g_lambda g_mu / g_nu and the obvious choice makes matters worse -- OR seek a combinatorial rule only on the jump <= 1 stratum, where polynomiality holds and a puzzle-style count is not yet excluded.

children.statement: HYPOTHESIS (2026-10-16 wake): the determinant/Pfaffian dichotomy is the SAME stratification as Q484's jump |nu|-max(|lambda|,|mu|), via Motegi's count of spectral parameters specialised to 1.
children.reason: The count is n-s, not n-r (Motegi states the distinction himself, L2790: 'r specifies the label cardinality, whereas s specifies the number of selected w-variables'). The wake note's n-r was read off the s=r stratum, where the two agree, and carried off it. Worse, n is a GAUGE parameter annihilated by stability eq:typeC-stability-s-ge-r, so n-r takes every value >=0 on the witness. The gauge-invariant residue s-r = |M|-|I| is a cardinality gap between an EVALUATION POINT and a BASIS LABEL (a row/column pair of Atilde), whereas the jump is a gap among THREE BASIS LABELS. Gaps in different slots of the same matrix: a one-coordinate match (both are cardinality gaps between increasing sequences in [N]; both vanish on M=I). Closed in under 30 min by the pre-registered gate.

children.statement: THEOREM. Call D a collision divisor if some tau with tau(M)<M satisfies Atilde_{M,I}|_D = Atilde_{tau M,I}|_D for all I. Then ord_D c^nu_{lambda,mu} >= 0 for ALL triples -- unconditionally, no jump hypothesis. The divisors w_a=1 (padding collision, via u-symmetry + stability), w_a=w_b (literal point collision), and w_a=-1 (via the symmetry Atilde(-w)=Atilde(w), sign exponent n(n+1)+2nN-2r = 0 mod 2) are all collision divisors. Proof: evaluate the defining identity at M=tau(nu); since tau(nu)<nu, the kappa-sum there is a sub-sum of the recursion's, so the numerator vanishes to matching order. ANSWERS the pre-registered u=-1 control: the u=-1 branch is NON-trivial -- a genuine second collision divisor with the same collapse map -- unlike the q=-1 collapse of 10-15.
children.approach: Identify the loci where two of the 2^N specialisation points COLLIDE, get a row collapse Atilde_{M,I}|_D = Atilde_{tau M,I}|_D from u-symmetry plus stability, and evaluate the defining identity at the collapsed point tau(nu) < nu so that its kappa-sum is a sub-sum of the recursion's.

children.statement: LEMMA A. For a<b, if {a,b} subset M and M\{a,b} not>= I then ord_{w_a w_b=1} Atilde_{M,I} >= 1. Proof: by motegi-branching-formula every surviving K satisfies K>=I, and if some surviving K missed {a,b} then K subset M\{a,b} would witness M\{a,b} >= I by Motegi's top-r criterion; so every surviving term carries the factor. Measured as an EQUALITY (10 pairs at N=2, 105 at N=3) but only the lower bound is used.
children.approach: Read the long-root factors off Motegi's branching formula term by term: pairs meeting K carry (1-w^{-1}w^{-1}), pairs inside M\K carry only the q-shifted factor; then use his top-r admissibility criterion applied to M\{a,b}.

children.statement: LEMMA. For nu>=lambda, nu>=mu: there exists a pair {a,b} subset nu with nu\{a,b} >= lambda and nu\{a,b} >= mu  <=>  |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) >= 2. Forward by cardinality; backward by deleting the two SMALLEST elements of nu, which leaves the top max(|lambda|,|mu|) elements untouched because Motegi's order compares only the top r. This is WHERE THE max COMES FROM: a pole needs the deleted pair to dominate BOTH lambda and mu, an 'and' whose negation is the 'or' that makes the criterion read min(|nu|-|lambda|,|nu|-|mu|)<=1.
children.approach: Pure combinatorics on Motegi's shifted-dominance order: forward by cardinality, backward by deleting the two SMALLEST elements of nu, which leaves the compared top-r window untouched.

children.statement: THEOREM (the 'if' half of Q484's conj:locus, previously only measured). If |nu|-max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= 1 then c^nu_{lambda,mu} has no pole on any long-root divisor w_a w_b = 1; with collision-divisors-no-pole and q-family-row-minimality it is a Laurent polynomial. Proof: induction along a linear extension. The hypothesis is INHERITED -- every kappa in the recursion has |kappa| <= |nu| <= max+1, so jump is monotone in |nu| along Motegi's order and no pole can be created below nu and inherited. Each term is handled by Lemma A: |nu|-2 < max(|lambda|,|mu|) <= |kappa| forces nu\{a,b} not>= kappa.
children.approach: Induction along a linear extension of Motegi's order, bounding ord_H of each term of the forward-substitution recursion by Lemma A; the jump hypothesis is inherited because kappa <= nu forces |kappa| <= |nu|.

children.statement: CONJECTURE, verified. The long-root pole divisor of c^nu_{lambda,mu} is exactly { H_ab : exists kappa with nu>=kappa>=lambda, kappa>=mu, {a,b} subset kappa, kappa\{a,b} >= lambda and >= mu } -- poles are CREATED at kappa (by jump-equals-pair-deletion read locally) and PROPAGATE upward through the recursion term c^kappa Atilde_{nu,kappa}. Verified 20/20 at N=2 and 115/115 at N=3 against SymPy, by an INDEPENDENT mechanism (pure subset combinatorics vs rational arithmetic + factor_list). Strictly stronger than the binary criterion: it names WHICH hyperplanes, with no free parameter. I first predicted only the created poles and the measurement corrected me (c^{(1,3)}_{0,0} at N=3 poles on w1w2=1 although 2 not in nu).
children.approach: Read Lemma A + the pair-deletion lemma LOCALLY at each kappa <= nu rather than only at nu, giving created-plus-propagated poles; compare the predicted hyperplane set against SymPy factor_list of the denominator, triple by triple.

children.statement: GAP. For D in the q-shifted family (q w_a w_b = 1, q w_a = w_b) I verify ord_D Atilde_{nu,nu} <= ord_D Atilde_{nu,I} for all I <= nu, which closes the case by the same induction. Verified at N=2,3 (9+9 divisors, no violation); NOT proved. Proved structural half: the E^C contribution to the order depends on M alone, not on I, so the statement reduces to the I-dependence of the W_{N,r} and bottom-boundary blocks of the branching formula.
children.approach: Check whether the diagonal entry minimises the order along its own row, which closes the case by the same induction; plus an attempt to prove it from the M-dependence of the normalisation E^C.

children.statement: GAP. The converse direction, jump >= 2 => a pole ACTUALLY occurs, needs non-vanishing: Lemma A is a divisibility statement and gives only lower bounds on orders. Requires the converse of Motegi's triangularity (M>=I => Atilde_{M,I} != 0; measured 84/84 in Q484) plus absence of conspiratorial cancellation among the surviving K-terms of the branching formula -- which is a finite computation per K-class, since each T_K is explicit. Status: measured (225/225 in Q484; exact-pole-divisor 20/20 + 115/115). Next prove session.
children.approach: Needs the leading coefficient on H_ab to be nonzero: the converse of Motegi's triangularity plus absence of cancellation among the surviving K-terms, which the branching formula makes a finite per-K-class computation.

children.statement: OPEN. Every number in Q484 and in the 2026-10-16 proof is type C. Nothing in the collision/long-root argument uses gamma=0 EXCEPT the sign count in collision-divisors-no-pole(iii): for WB the extra prefactor prod_k (1+u_k^{-1})^{-1} is NOT invariant under u -> -u (it has a pole at u_k=-1). So the u=-1 collision divisor is exactly where type B may differ from type C. Sharper than Q484's open thread 3, and cheap to test; type-B M-smallness is defined at L1346 in the same file.
